subject: SLA: stability buffer pilot & credit cap discussion
messages:
From: Sophie Clarke <sophie@fathomapps.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@fathomapps.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA uplift & credit anchoring for pilot

Diego — thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to move the pilot forward, but procurement wants to get SLA language clarified before we sign the pilot SOW. Two items they asked me to raise: 

1) Uptime commitment: we see your standard template lists 99.95% for hosted inference. For our pilot budget we need a temporary floor — procurement is proposing 99.5% for the first 90 days while we ramp traffic.

2) Monthly credits: they want a clear cap and a single pool rather than line-item credits for multiple triggers. For predictability, they prefer a fixed monthly cap (a percentage of the invoice) rather than an open-ended remedy ladder.

Can you share how Redwood normally handles a short-term pilot exception like this and whether you can provide a short amendment (one page) that pins the pilot floor and a capped credit pool? Also, if you have the measurement method for uptime (how you calculate the percentage and what windows you use), that would help expedite review.

Thanks — happy to sync on a quick call if easier.

— Sophie
Sophie Clarke
Head of Infrastructure, FathomApps
---
Attachments: none
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Sophie Clarke <sophie@fathomapps.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA uplift & credit anchoring for pilot

Sophie — thanks for outlining procurement’s needs. Looping Laura (legal) and Marissa (solutions) so we can get a short, signable amendment in front of you. High level proposal from our side: 

- Pilot stability buffer: temporary uptime floor of 99.5% for the first 90 days following go-live. This is a bounded exception to our standard template (99.95%).
- Remedy structure: single monthly remedy pool capped at 20% of the recurring invoice for the pilot month. Credits are applied as a rebate on the following month’s invoice.
- Measurement: platform-side availability calculation using rolling daily windows aggregated to monthly (downtime measured in total minutes across the month / total available minutes). We’ll provide the exact query and sample output.

Couple of notes / asks from our side: 
- We typically exclude scheduled maintenance windows with 48hr advance notice; please confirm if Fathom needs different blackout rules for planned maintenance.
- For auditability, we’ll attach a one-page metrics spec (how we compute the numerator/denominator) and a draft amendment (SLA-amendment-draft-v1.pdf).

If this sounds directionally correct, Laura and Marissa — can you 1) review the attached one-pager and amendment and 2) mark any legal redlines? Sophie — if procurement has a preferred cap (percentage) or wants a shorter/longer pilot length, tell us and we’ll iterate.

Next steps: I can schedule a 30-minute procurement + legal sync tomorrow morning if that helps.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

Thanks Diego — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed the high-level ask and has two quick counterpoints: 

- Cap: they’d prefer a 15% monthly cap rather than 20% (they’re trying to limit downside while the pilot proves stability).
- Measurement & maintenance carveout: they want the maintenance carveout called out in the amendment and the measurement documented as a 5-minute rolling window for incident detection, with a 5-minute suppression for transient network flaps. They also asked for a brief definition of what constitutes a service-impacting incident (basically full API rejection or >50% error rate on a 5-minute rollup).

I’m pasting procurement’s note below for completeness.

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sophie / procurement. We can accept the 15% cap for the pilot and will add explicit maintenance carveout language to the amendment. Quick clarifications so Laura can prepare redlines: 

- Final pilot terms we’ll put in the amendment: 90-day pilot from go-live; temporary uptime floor 99.5%; single monthly remedy pool capped at 15% of the monthly recurring invoice; credits applied as invoice rebate on the following invoice cycle.
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance with >=48hr notice excluded; any emergency maintenance will be documented and tracked but not automatically excluded (we’ll discuss thresholds).
- Measurement method: we’ll publish the exact SQL and a sample month export showing available minutes and downtime minutes. For the amendment, we’ll reference the metric spec (uptime-metrics-spec.xlsx) and include a short definition of a service-impacting incident (>=50% errors across all endpoints on a 5-minute rollup or sustained full-API rejection).

Laura — could you 1) draft redlines to SLA-amendment-draft-v1.pdf to reflect the 15% cap and maintenance carveout, and 2) confirm if the credit application language should include a manual review step before credits are applied (we typically automate but legal sometimes prefers a 10-business-day dispute window).

Sophie / procurement — if that matches your expectation I’ll send an updated amendment and the sample metrics export today and propose a 30-minute call tomorrow at 09:30 PT to sign off.

Thanks all,
Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
